reviews.one_line_contribution: That retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions are the same kind of device — inference-time distribution-concentrators that buy pass@1 by deleting reachable solutions rather than adding new ones — and that because they concentrate onto *different* modes, stacking them compounds the coverage loss while sub-adding the pass@1 gain, so the complementarity is only harvestable by splitting conditioning across rollouts (P1) rather than across prompt slots.
reviews.closest_prior_work: The proposal names arXiv 2605.28224 as a partial collision and handles it honestly, but the work that most threatens novelty is the one it never cites: the pass@k-boundary literature on RLVR (Yue et al. 2025, 'Does RL Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity Beyond the Base Model?'), together with Large Language Monkeys (2407.21787) and the sharpening formalization (Huang et al., 2412.01951). Those papers *invented* the exact instrument this proposal presents as its contribution — per-instance solve-probability pools, unbiased pass@k, solve-set nesting, and the sharpening-vs-new-capability adjudication — and used it to show that a pass@1-improving intervention narrows the solve set. Coverage accounting is therefore a standard instrument here, and porting it from weight-space to context-conditioning is a transfer, not a new measurement idea; the proposal's framing of 'the coverage accounting' as its own novel contribution (Related Work cluster 4, 'none establishes the training-free, inference-time analogue') overstates the gap, since 2412.10684 already reported retrieval degrading self-consistency and 2505.16067 already gave the mechanism (experience-following). What genuinely survives is narrow: the optimizer-side replication plus the JSD mode-identity test (Prediction 6). That is a real increment, but it is one figure's worth, and it rests entirely on GEPA clearing precheck P-b, which the proposal's own Risk 6 flags as doubtful on an 8B agent.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline concentration result is largely guaranteed by the design, and the one arm that would adjudicate the mechanism is confounded. Three compounding problems. (1) Precheck P-a selects the bank on exactly the axis the hypothesis is about: 'we enrich the bank until it passes' a >=5pt dev pass@1 gain. Among candidate banks, the one maximizing dev pass@1 is the most concentrating one, and its dev-selected >=5pt gain will regress on test — so Prediction 1's 'crossover k* <= 8' becomes easy to satisfy by winner's curse alone, with no coverage destruction required. (2) Risk-mitigation 2 filters the test pool to instances with unconditioned pass@1 in the 30-60% band. That filter deletes precisely the instances where NEW lives (A0 rate near zero), so Prediction 2's 'NEW < 4% of the test set' is partly built in by construction; and it pushes A0's pass@8 toward ceiling, so Prediction 1's 'advantage <= 2 points by k=8' follows from arithmetic compression of a saturating curve rather than from lost coverage. (3) A4, billed as 'the decisive mechanism arm,' cannot decide anything, because temperature-induced diversity is not the same object as conditioning-induced strategy diversity, and matching a scalar summary (mean distinct strategies within 5%) does not match the distribution. If A4 fails to restore pass@8 — the predicted outcome — the result is equally well explained by 'hot sampling produces incoherent, low-quality strategies' as by 'memory shifted the mode.' The falsification path is asymmetric: A4 can kill the mode-shift claim but cannot confirm it. Secondary but checkable: Measurement (e) asserts 'every quantitative prediction above is stated at or beyond' the ~4.5-point MDE. This is false for at least three. Prediction 8 asks for a >=2-point O3-over-O2 pass@1 gap; Prediction 7's sub-additivity margin is 2 points on a three-arm composite whose SE is roughly sqrt(3)x1.7 ~ 3 points; and Prediction 1's k=8 equivalence band is 4 points, where equivalence testing needs more power than superiority, not less. The paper's coupling claim — its declared spine after conceding the memory half to 2605.28224 — is thus stated at effect sizes the design admits it cannot resolve. Finally, on significance: pass@k presumes an oracle verifier, which HotpotQA/MuSiQue agents do not have at deployment. Coverage loss is a diagnostic, not a shipped loss, and the constructive corollary P1 only becomes a method once a selection rule exists; P2 is one arm, not an answer.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Five concrete changes, in order of load. (a) Remove the outcome-axis selection: fix the bank and the GEPA budget by a pre-registered rule that does not condition on pass@1 gain, report the full precheck sweep, and treat bank strength as a measured moderator rather than an entry gate — or, if the gate is kept, use a dev split for selection and a fully disjoint pool for the reported pass@1 delta so the winner's curse is not smuggled into k*. (b) Drop the 30-60% pass@1 instance filter, or report NEW/LOST on the unfiltered pool as the primary and the filtered pool only for curve legibility; as written the filter excises the region where the NEW category can exist. (c) Make A4 two-sided and quality-controlled: also cool A0 down until its diversity matches A1's (does low-diversity A0 lose the same instances?), and add a quality-matched arm (e.g. min-p or best-of-n filtered hot sampling) so a null in A4 cannot be absorbed by 'temperature diversity is bad diversity.' Without this, the mode-shift claim is not testable by A4. (d) Restate Predictions 1, 7 and 8 at effects the design can detect, or raise n per instance for the O-arms specifically — the coupling predictions are the spine and currently sit under the MDE. (e) Add the decoding-diversity portfolio control (below) and commit to a concrete verifier-free selection rule so the portfolio result maps onto a deployment metric. A sixth, cheaper fix: run MIPROv2 on the decisive E1 arms. 'Concentration is the common currency' of prompt optimization is an n=1 claim about GEPA's reflective operator otherwise, and Risk 7 concedes this without repairing it.
reviews.missing_baseline: A diversity-only portfolio control: k rollouts of the *unconditioned* agent spread over varied decoding settings and/or paraphrased-but-uninformative instructions (a prompt ensemble), at matched total tokens, run through the identical pass@k pipeline. This is the standard cheap coverage booster, and it is the direct competitor to P1. If mixed-temperature or mixed-paraphrase A0 reaches P1's interior optimum, Prediction 9 shows only that heterogeneity helps — a known result — and nothing about memory and the optimizer occupying complementary modes; the constructive corollary, the paper's payload, then collapses to 'diversify your rollouts.' P1's stated endpoints (A0, A1, O1) do not cover this, because all three are homogeneous-conditioning endpoints. Two lesser omissions a reviewer would also press: (i) a static generic few-shot arm (fixed hand-picked exemplars, token-matched), which is what practitioners actually compare memory against and which A3's off-task decoy does not stand in for — A3 varies relevance, not experience-versus-demonstration; (ii) MIPROv2, acknowledged as cut in Risk 7.
reviews.preprint_collision: The check is better than most and should be credited: it names a genuine collision (2605.28224), declines to argue it away, explicitly drops the 'memory reduces diversity' claim, states what survives, discloses that the search budget ran out before three named memory titles and before any OpenReview sweep, and concedes a nontrivial probability that a pass@k-with-and-without-memory figure already exists. That is honest practice. Two things undercut it. First, the unswept region is exactly where the residual claim lives: 'MemCollab, ParamMem, Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory' are 2026 memory papers, and a pass@k curve in any of them removes the memory half outright, leaving only the GEPA-coupling half — which Risk 6 concedes may never clear its own precheck. The gap in the search coincides with the load-bearing claim, which is the worst place for it. Second, the check searches only the memory/diversity neighborhood and misses the coverage-accounting neighborhood entirely: Yue et al. 2025 on the RLVR pass@k boundary, Large Language Monkeys (2407.21787), and the sharpening formalization (2412.01951) are not mentioned anywhere in the proposal, yet they own the instrument the proposal advertises as its methodological contribution. A reviewer will read cluster 4's 'none establishes the training-free, inference-time analogue' as a fair statement about the intervention and an unfair one about the measurement. No verdict-changing scoop is demonstrated here, but the claim of an unoccupied methodological gap is not established either.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A pre-registered, sampling-aware audit protocol claiming that retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions are the same kind of device — distribution-concentration, not information-addition — such that each buys pass@1 by deleting solvable instances via mode shift (not sharpening), stacking them compounds the loss while sub-adding the gain, and the only harvestable complementarity is across rollouts rather than across prompt slots.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two threats. (1) arXiv 2605.28224 ("When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?"), which the proposal itself concedes owns the memory-side causal story in the same regime; what survives is genuinely narrower than the Title advertises — coverage bookkeeping, a temperature control, and the optimizer half. (2) The training-time collapse literature (2509.06941, 2509.04784) plus GEPA/MIPROv2's own objective: a search that greedily maximizes single-sample validation accuracy over a fixed sampler is, by construction, a concentration device. Predicting that O1 loses pass@k is close to definitionally true, so the optimizer half — the part the proposal makes its spine — is an unsurprising positive, not a discovery. The portfolio corollary is weaker still: prompt/condition ensembling to raise coverage is folklore in the repeated-sampling literature (their own cited 2505.12938 runs this direction), and Prediction 9 is nearly entailed by Prediction 6 — if A1 and O1 concentrate onto modes with mean JSD ≥ 0.4 and each crosses over by k=8, the union of their solve sets beating any single arm is arithmetic, not evidence.
reviews.strongest_objection: The coverage decomposition is biased toward its own predicted answer by the instance-selection rule. Risk factor 2 selects the test pool to have unconditioned pass@1 in the 30–60% band. NEW is defined as "A0 never solves in n=16, treatment sometimes does" — at a true A0 rate of 0.30 the probability of zero successes in 16 draws is ~0.003, so the NEW cell is emptied by the sampling design, while LOST ("treatment never solves in 16") is thresholded on the treatment arm, which the filter does not constrain at all. The filter is applied to A0 only, so the decomposition is structurally asymmetric: Prediction 2 (NEW < 4% of the test set, LOST/NEW ≥ 2) is close to guaranteed by the pool construction plus n=16 resolution regardless of whether memory or the optimizer removes any solution. The Jeffreys posterior and split-half checks quantify the noise in the labels but do not touch the selection asymmetry that generates the predicted ratio. Second, mutually reinforcing: the prechecks demand a ≥5-point (memory) and ≥3-point (GEPA) pass@1 gain and say "we enrich the bank / extend the GEPA budget until it passes" on a 150-instance dev split. That is selecting each component for maximal single-sample concentration on dev — precisely the property whose consequences are then measured on test — and it directly contradicts the track's own measured starting position (memory fixed zero and broke six to seven; the optimizer's gain was redistribution, not accuracy). The conditions under which the study runs at all are the conditions that manufacture its conclusion. Third, the paper's actual centre is underpowered by its own arithmetic: stated SE is ~1.7 points on a single paired pass@k difference (MDE ~4.5 points), yet Prediction 7 is a three-arm difference-of-differences with a 2-point slack and Prediction 8 asks for a 2-point O3-over-O2 gap and a 0.1 JSD shift. A contrast of contrasts carries roughly 2.5–3 points of SE here, so the coupling claims — the half the proposal says degrades gracefully into the contribution — cannot be resolved by this design in either direction.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: 1) Stop conditioning the pool on A0. Either select instances by a conditioning-blind criterion (e.g. pooled solve rate across all arms, or stratified sampling over the full difficulty range) or abandon the NEW/LOST thresholds as primary and make the headline a continuous, symmetric statistic: the paired shift in per-instance solve probability (Δ log-odds, or the signed mass moving off/onto zero under the Jeffreys posterior), reported over the unfiltered test set. Report NEW/LOST as a secondary readout with the selection-induced floor stated explicitly. 2) Add a temperature-matched A0 arm alongside A4. As written, if A4 fails to restore coverage, "memory shifted the mode" is confounded with "hot decoding degrades ReAct tool-call coherence"; only A0 at the same temperature separates them, and this is cheap. 3) Restore the top-3 injection-volume arm. The token-matched decoy A3 spans content, not dosage, and the track's own prior result names volume as the causal lever; without a dose axis the finding may be "more conditioning tokens concentrate," which is a dosage story, not a common currency. 4) Fix the precheck before looking at anything: pre-register the enrichment procedure and its stopping rule, or drop the gate and report what a standard ExpeL-style bank and a fixed GEPA budget actually do, including the case where the honest answer is the track's own null. 5) Power the coupling contrasts — restate Predictions 7 and 8 at ≥5 points, or reallocate rollouts from the descriptive arms to O2/O3 so a difference-of-differences is detectable.
reviews.missing_baseline: GEPA run against a multi-sample objective — candidate selection on pass@4 (or on solve-set coverage) instead of single-sample validation accuracy, then pushed through the identical coverage pipeline. The Related Work section diagnoses the problem as the optimizer's objective being sampling-unaware, but no arm changes the objective, so the plan cannot distinguish "prompt optimization is intrinsically a concentration device" (the paper's thesis) from "pass@1-greedy search concentrates, and a two-line change to the selection metric fixes it" — the latter is both more likely and cheaper to test than the portfolio machinery, and a reviewer will demand it because the proposal itself supplies the argument for it. Secondarily, the cut top-3 injection-volume arm (the dose control the track's own prior results single out) and MIPROv2 as a second optimizer, without which "prompt optimization" means "GEPA's reflective operator."
reviews.preprint_collision: Unusually honest and above the norm for this exercise: it names a genuine partial collision (2605.28224), concedes the memory-side claim to it rather than arguing it away, reorganizes the proposal around what survives, states the remaining delta concretely (solve-set measurement, diversity-matched control, falsifiable decoy prediction, no optimizer), and admits an exhausted budget with three uncharacterized titles and no OpenReview sweep. That earns credit. But the check is thin exactly where the surviving novelty lives. The searches cover memory-and-diversity and training-time collapse thoroughly, and the optimizer side is represented only by MIPROv2/GEPA themselves — there is no search at all for prompt or instruction optimization evaluated under pass@k, for diversity- or coverage-aware prompt search, or for few-shot demonstrations reducing solve-set coverage in code/agent generation, and only one lexical-diversity ICL citation (2404.16807) stands in for that whole area. The portfolio corollary is likewise unsearched: heterogeneous prompt/condition ensembling to raise pass@k is established practice in the repeated-sampling literature and the proposal cites only 2505.12938 as a "counterpoint" rather than as a coverage-ensembling precedent. So both halves the proposal now claims as its own — optimizer-as-concentrator and the portfolio fix — rest on an unsearched novelty claim, which is a weakness, not a neutral. Also, the surviving contribution is now one preprint's follow-up analysis away from being fully scooped, and the proposal's own Risk 1 concedes this.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A sampling-aware audit arguing that retrieved-experience memory and GEPA-optimized instructions are the same kind of device — distribution concentrators that buy pass@1 by destroying solve-set coverage rather than adding it — so stacking them compounds the coverage loss while pass@1 gains sub-add, and the complementarity should instead be harvested by splitting the rollout budget across differently-conditioned prompts (arms A1/O1/O2/O3 and the P1 portfolio).
reviews.closest_prior_work: arXiv 2605.28224 ("When Does Memory Help Multi-Trajectory Inference for Tool-Use LLM Agents?"), which the proposal itself concedes owns the memory-side claim in the same regime (retrieved experience, tool-use agents, multi-trajectory inference, diversity-vs-efficiency tradeoff attributed to positive priors inducing consistency). The concession is honest but costly: it removes A1 from the novelty ledger and leaves the paper standing on the optimizer/coupling half (O1/O2/O3, predictions 6-8), which is exactly the half with the weakest statistical footing. Second threat, and the one the proposal never engages: the prompt-ensemble / diverse-prompt pass@k literature (DiVeRSe; Li et al. 2022 "Making Language Models Better Reasoners"; the proposal's own cited 2505.12938 on exploiting LLM inconsistency to boost pass@k) already establishes that heterogeneous prompts over a fixed sample budget beat homogeneous prompting at pass@k. P1 is therefore a re-derivation of a known ensembling result in agent clothing, and the "constructive corollary" that the proposal calls its payload is the least novel component in the plan. Also relevant: 2509.06941 / 2509.04784 make pass@1-up/pass@k-down the default expectation a reader now brings to any conditioning intervention, so the inference-time analogue reads as confirmation rather than discovery.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline coverage result is largely manufactured by the sampling frame and the gating procedure, and most of the numeric predictions sit below the design's own detection threshold. (1) Risk factor 2 states the instance pool is selected for unconditioned pass@1 in the 30-60% band. NEW is defined as "A0 never solves in n=16"; an instance with A0 rate >=0.30 fails to solve 16 times with probability 0.7^16 ~ 0.3%. So the pool construction all but excludes the instances where NEW can occur, while LOST (treatment kills a 30-60% instance) remains fully available. Prediction 2 (NEW < 4% of the test set, LOST/NEW >= 2) is close to entailed by the selection rule rather than discovered by the experiment, and the "coverage nesting" headline inherits that. (2) Section (e) states SE ~ 1.7 points on a paired pass@k difference and ~4.5 points detectable at 80% power, yet prediction 7's key contrast gain(O2) < gain(A1)+gain(O1)-2 involves three noisy paired quantities (SE ~ 2.9 on the contrast) tested against a 2-point margin; prediction 8 asserts a 2-point pass@1 gap and a 0.1 JSD gap with no noise floor stated for a difference of JSDs; prediction 1's k=8 equivalence at a 4-point margin needs a 95% CI half-width (~3.3 points) narrower than the margin, which will hold only if the point estimate lands near zero. The coupling half of the paper — now the spine, per the collision check — is thus predominantly powered to return "inconclusive," and the proposal has pre-registered honest escape hatches for exactly that. (3) The theory has little positive content beyond "conditioning lowers output entropy": the proposal itself predicts the length-matched decoy A3 reproduces up to half of A1's coverage loss, conceding that up to half the effect is generic context load; and sub-additivity of two gains on a bounded metric targeting overlapping easy instances (prediction 7) is the default null expectation, not a risky claim.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Four changes, in order of importance. (a) Add an entropy-matched unconditioned arm — A0 sampled at a temperature lowered until its per-instance strategy diversity matches A1's — as the mirror of A4. A4 alone is confounded: raising temperature under memory degrades per-sample coherence, so "coverage does not return" is equally explained by hot-sampling damage as by mode shift. The low-temperature A0 is the decisive test: if it reproduces A1's pass@1 gain and coverage loss, the entire common-currency thesis reduces to "conditioning reduces sampling entropy," which is not an ICLR contribution. (b) Stratify the test pool by A0 solve rate and include an explicit hard stratum where A0 pass@1 is near zero, reporting NEW/LOST per stratum; otherwise the decomposition cannot see the only instances where NEW is possible. (c) Re-budget for the coupling claims: fewer instances at larger n (e.g. 150 x n=32) on E1, and restate predictions 7-9 at thresholds above the realized MDE, replacing the near-certain sub-additivity statement with a pre-registered interaction test on per-instance solve-probability logits that could plausibly come out super-additive. (d) Drop or pre-register the "enrich the bank / extend GEPA budget until it passes" remediation in the prechecks: as written it is an unbounded dev-set search that conditions the whole study on components that already concentrate, and it tunes away the track's own starting observation that a full seven-item bank fixed zero items and broke six or seven. Also run A3/A4 on Qwen2.5-14B; as scheduled, every mechanism claim rests on one model in one environment.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two. Primary: the entropy/diversity-matched unconditioned agent (A0 with temperature lowered until strategy diversity matches A1's) — the null model in which memory does nothing except reduce sampling entropy. Without it, every coverage loss attributed to "memory as mode shift" has a one-knob alternative explanation, and A4 (which only moves the temperature in the other direction, and is admitted in risk factor 5 as possibly unachievable) cannot supply it. Secondary: a static, relevant few-shot ICL arm — seven fixed gold demonstrations drawn once from the training split, token-matched, no retrieval. A3 is a decoy from a disjoint task family, so the design has no arm separating "retrieved, query-specific experience" from "any relevant demonstrations," which is the comparison the ExpeL/ReasoningBank literature would demand and the one that decides whether the paper is about memory at all.
reviews.preprint_collision: The best part of the submission and still not sufficient. It is unusually honest — it names arXiv 2605.28224 as a genuine partial collision, declines to argue it away, restructures the contribution around what survives, and states its own caveats (search budget exhausted before three borderline titles; OpenReview 2026 unswept; a nontrivial probability that a pass@k-with-and-without-memory figure already exists). Judged as evidence of novelty, however, it is asymmetric in the wrong direction: it is thorough on the memory side, which the proposal has now demoted, and effectively empty on the two things the paper now rests on. There is no reported search for prompt-optimization-side diversity or pass@k effects (DSPy/MIPROv2/GEPA candidates overfitting to single-sample validation, instruction search and output diversity) even though "does the optimizer carry the same signature" is the declared spine; and there is no search for prompt-ensemble / diverse-prompt pass@k work, which is the direct precedent for the P1 portfolio result. Cluster (5) cites 2404.16807 for lexical ICL diversity and 2505.12938 as a "counterpoint," but never asks whether the portfolio claim is already established. An unsearched load-bearing half is a weakness, not a neutral, and the admitted possibility that the coverage figure already exists means the memory half should be treated as replication in the writeup rather than as a finding.
